Subject: Recap & asks from today

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and a short list of next steps so we can map the right deployment path (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).

What I heard:
- Primary use will process PHI (patient notes + transcriptions) for clinical summarization and quality checks.
- Legal requires a signed BAA before any PHI processing.
- Retention policy: 7 years for audit records; need logs and access reports.
- Expected initial throughput: ~50 concurrent requests, bursty during EHR sync windows.

Asks for you (and your procurement/security team):
1) Confirm BAA scope items that are must-haves vs negotiables.
2) Any specific regional/data residency mandates?
3) Timeline for procurement / legal review (target month?).

What we need to provide to you now (I can share under NDA):
- SOC 2 Type II summary and redacted report excerpt (we typically share under NDA).
- Pen test summary and remediation log.
- Deployment recommendations and SLOs for Dedicated vs Private in context of PHI.

Attaching my quick call notes (DiscoveryNotes-ClinicCare-20270207.pdf). I will loop in our security and solutions leads to provide the evidence and recommendation.

Proposed next step: 30-minute technical follow-up with Marcus (solutions) + your security at a time that works this week. Are you available Thu or Fri?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Would suggest we propose a deployment that balances speed-to-prod with compliance (e.g., Dedicated with BAA for immediate rollout, with option to migrate to Private if legal requires data residency/air-gapped environment).

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-02-08T17:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap & asks from today

Monica / Marcus —

Thanks for the context. Short answers up front, then supporting details.

1) BAA scope and recommended deployment
- We can sign a BAA for an enterprise customer on Hosted in limited cases; however, Hosted runs on shared infrastructure and requires careful scoping (no data retention beyond request lifecycle, strong contractual controls). For a customer that requires long audit log retention (7 years) and tight data isolation, our recommended path is Dedicated (isolated GPU pools, logical isolation, SLA) or Private VPC / on-prem for the strictest controls and residency.
- Recommendation for ClinicCare: start with Dedicated + BAA to meet procurement speed and throughput needs, with a migration plan to Private if legal or regulator mandates physical residency / air-gapped controls.

2) Evidence we can share immediately (under NDA)
- SOC 2 Type II redacted excerpt: includes control mapping for access, change management, and incident response. (file: redwood_soc2_excerpt.pdf)
- Penetration test executive summary & remediation log (file: pen_test_summary.txt)
- High-level architecture diagram showing encryption in transit and at rest, KMS options, and audit logging endpoints — Marcus can prepare a short slide.
- Logs & retention: we can ship audit logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket or a secure archival store for long-term retention; we also support log export for eDiscovery.

3) Practical notes for the call
- Marcus should cover network/topology options (Dedicated vs Private) and migration approach.
- Legal/procurement typically ask for: BAA draft, SOC2 report under NDA, pen test summary, and SLA language for uptime.

I'll attach the SOC2 excerpt and pen test summary for you to send under NDA. Marcus — can you prepare a one-slide architecture comparison and a proposed Dedicated config (GPU type, concurrency limits, autoscale policy) before Thu morning?

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_soc2_excerpt.pdf; pen_test_summary.txt
